mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'the difference between the number of X and Y' as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order of names. Without this, the model may treat the difference as an absolute value and lose sign information.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement describes a difference between two persons' counts.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between A and B' as |A - B| instead of A - B.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements like 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N). Without this, the model may reverse the direction of the relationship or mis-handle 'fewer' statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses 'more' or 'fewer' to compare two persons.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 5 fewer than B' as A = B + 5 instead of A = B - 5.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement 'A has N items' appears, set A's current count to N at that moment, overwriting any previous value. Without this, earlier assignments might be incorrectly treated as immutable.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement gives an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Keeping an earlier count for A even after a later statement says 'A has 7 items'.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the order given; apply each transfer immediately before evaluating any later relational statements, using the updated counts. Without this, later equations may be evaluated with stale values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any transfer (unconditional) or relational statement that follows a transfer.
mathgap.example: Evaluating 'B has 3 more than A' before applying a prior transfer from C to A.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, translate them into (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order on each side. Without this, the model may collapse the equation to a single variable assignment and lose a term.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence states that one difference equals another difference.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A - B = C' as A = B + C, ignoring D.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by a numeric operation other than direct assignment or transfer (e.g., multiplication, subtraction), apply that operation to the current count. Without this, the model may leave the count unchanged or apply the wrong arithmetic.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement says a person's count is increased, decreased, or multiplied by a specific factor.
mathgap.example: Leaving a count unchanged after a statement like 'A's items increase by 2 times'.

mathgap.title: Split All Items Equally Among Recipients
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two or more recipients, set each recipient's count to the original count divided equally (integer division, assuming divisibility). Without this, the model may distribute incorrectly or forget to zero the original holder.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence describes a split of one person's items among others.
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient the full original amount instead of a share.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Among Group
mathgap.principle: When a group of persons redistributes their items to ensure each ends up with the same amount, compute the total of the group, divide by the number of members, and set each member to that equal share. Without this, the model may leave counts uneven or mis‑allocate the total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says two or more people redistribute their items to equalize.
mathgap.example: Leaving one person with more items after a redistribution statement.

mathgap.title: Comprehensive Constraint Extraction
mathgap.principle: Collect all statements that involve any variable, not only those that mention the queried person, before solving. Without this, the model may stop after a subset of constraints and miss necessary relationships.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, gather every equation, transfer, and modification from the problem text.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a transfer that does not involve the target person, leading to an incorrect final count.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer Evaluation
mathgap.principle: For statements that condition a transfer on a count threshold (e.g., 'If X has more than N items, X will transfer all items to Y'), evaluate the condition using the current count at that point; if true, move all items from X to Y (X becomes 0, Y increases by that amount). Perform this immediately, before any later statements. Without this, the model may treat the transfer as unconditional or ignore the condition.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever an 'if' clause conditions a transfer on a person's current count.
mathgap.example: Treating a conditional transfer as unconditional, moving items even when the condition is false.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to thinking of 'difference' as a magnitude, ignoring order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of names and compute X - Y, not |X - Y|.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model processes relational statements first and forgets that transfers change counts immediately.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer as soon as it appears, before any later statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats 'has N items' as a permanent fact rather than a mutable state.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Update the person's count whenever a transfer or modification occurs, even after a direct assignment.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model simplifies the equation incorrectly, dropping one side of the equality.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate difference equalities fully as (A - B) = (C - D).

mathgap.description: Incomplete processing of problem statements: stopping after a subset of constraints or ignoring many statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may focus only on statements involving the queried person and miss indirect constraints.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Extract and consider every statement before solving.
